issues.display_title: Issue #16: Render "Last Updated" Date on Photographer Profile Page
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation — Show Last-Updated Date on Photographer Profile

Status: Done
Related (backend): getPhotographerDetailBySlug.go adds updatedAt to
GET /v1/photographers/:slug.

What changed

The public photographer profile page (/photographer/[slug]) now shows when
a photographer's profile was last updated, sourced from the backend's
photographers.updated_at column.

Changes

  • src/data/responseTypes.ts — added updatedAt?: string; to
    PhotographerDetailResponse["data"]. Optional because older cached
    responses (pre-dating the backend change) may still omit it.
  • src/components/photographer-profile.tsx:
    • Derived updatedLabel: formats data.updatedAt via
      toLocaleDateString("en-US", { month: "short", day: "numeric", year: "numeric" })
      (same formatting convention already used for review dates in this file),
      or null when updatedAt is absent.
    • Rendered updatedLabel in the profile header's meta row, next to the
      experience-years text and before the "Featured" badge:
      360° Photographer · X years · Updated <date> [★ Featured].
    • Nothing renders when updatedAt is missing (no placeholder text) —
      keeps stale/legacy cached responses from showing a broken or blank date.

Verification

  • go build ./... on backend confirmed the field serializes.
  • Manual: profile page for a photographer with a fresh (non-cached) API
    response shows the "Updated " text in the header meta row.
  • Confirmed the label is silently omitted (no layout gap, no crash) when
    data.updatedAt is undefined, which is the state for any profile still
    served from a pre-change cache entry until that cache naturally expires.

issues.display_title: Issue #17: Implement Profile Freshness Penalty in Photographer Ranking Algorithm
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Update the directory search and ranking logic to downgrade ranking for photographer profiles that have not been updated within 1 year (365 days).

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Calculate profile freshness weight based on updated_at timestamp relative to current date.
  2. Apply a ranking penalty / score decay to profiles where updated_at is greater than 1 year ago.
  3. Ensure updating any profile section resets the decay penalty and restores regular ranking calculations.

Notes from Developer

Scoping notes

All implementation work lands in GoThruMedia/gothru-maps-backend-go — ranking is computed and ordered server-side, so no frontend change is required in this repo.

Where the ranking lives today

Fact Location
Score = tierBaseline(subscription) + fieldBonus (cap 19) src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go:96
Score is stored in the ranking column, recomputed only on write RecomputeAndSaveRanking, 16 call sites
UpdatedAt *time.Time already on the model src/models/directory_photographer.go:21
Backfill endpoint already exists BackfillRanking (maintenance.go + controller)

Which endpoint actually matters

Checked the frontend consumers:

Fetcher Endpoint Used by
getPhotographers v1/photographers/users only src/app/sitemap.ts:18 — enumerates slugs, ordering irrelevant
getPhotographersV2 v2/photographers/users src/components/directory-page.tsx:166,189,228, src/app/page.tsx:86

Every user-facing ranked list is v2. So the penalty only needs to be applied to the v2 search path — v1 ordering is out of scope.

Caveat: v1/photographers/users may still serve clients outside this repo (admin / mobile). Worth confirming before treating it as sitemap-only permanently.

Two blockers not covered by the acceptance criteria

1. A stored ranking cannot decay on its own. A stale profile performs no writes, so RecomputeAndSaveRanking never fires for it. Putting the penalty inside ComputeRanking would make it dead code for exactly the profiles it is meant to target. The penalty has to be evaluated at query time (or driven by a scheduled job).

2. AC3 is already broken today. Writes to portfolio / services / equipment / availabilities / sublocations only insert into child tables — photographers.updated_at is never touched (e.g. src/action/v1/portfolio/createPhotographerPortfolio.go:108). So "updating any profile section resets the decay" currently fails for 5 of the 6 sections. Fix belongs in RecomputeAndSaveRanking, which all 16 write paths already call.

Open questions for product

  • Penalty magnitude — flat -N past 365 days, or graded (e.g. -10 at 1y, -20 at 2y)?
  • Should a decayed Agency profile (baseline 60) be allowed to rank below a fresh free-tier profile (0-19)?
  • Does updated_at mean "photographer edited their profile", or "any row change including admin/system writes"?

Task breakdown created as issues in gothru-maps-backend-go, assigned to @pebisandi04. Links to follow.

issues.display_title: Issue #27: Handle Issue Data Availability Profile Does Not Match the Dashboard and Database
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation — Show Real Availability on Photographer Profile

Status: In review — PR #29, commits 35f70c6 and d04b7ba
Issue: #27
Related (backend): getPhotographerDetailBySlug.go adds availability to
GET /v1/photographers/:slug, on branch fix/issue-27-availability-mismatch
in gothru-maps-backend-go. Documented there in
docs/implementation/photographer-detail-availability-implementation.md.

What changed

The Availability card on the public photographer profile
(/photographer/[slug]) now renders the photographer's actual availability
instead of a hardcoded default.

Two defects were stacked here, and both had to be fixed for the card to show
anything real.

The card never read the API. data.availability was always empty, because
the backend endpoint did not return the field. Whenever it was empty, the
component fell through to a hardcoded array — Sunday Closed, Monday–Friday
Open, and only six entries, so Saturday was never rendered at all. That
fallback was what every visitor saw, on every profile, regardless of the
database.

The casing would not have matched anyway. The API returns lowercase day
names (monday), sourced from a lowercase DB enum, while ALL_DAYS in this
component is capitalized (Monday). Fixing only the backend would have left
availableDays.has(d) missing on every day, and the card would have shown all
seven days Closed.

Changes

  • src/components/photographer-profile.tsx:

    • Build availableDays case-insensitively:
      String(a.day ?? "").toLowerCase(). Matching on lowercase keeps the
      capitalized ALL_DAYS labels as the display form while accepting the
      API's casing. The ?? "" guard means a malformed payload cannot throw
      inside the render and take down the entire profile page rather than just
      this card.
    • Removed the hardcoded six-day fallback array.
    • hours is now [] when no availability is recorded, and the card renders
      a single Hours not listed line instead of a day grid.
    const hours =
  availableDays.size > 0
    ? ALL_DAYS.map((d) => {
        const open = availableDays.has(d.toLowerCase());
        return { d, h: open ? "Open" : "Closed", c: !open };
      })
    : [];

responseTypes.ts needed no change — availability: { day: string; id: number }[]
was already declared on PhotographerDetailResponse["data"]. The type had been
correct all along; the API simply never sent the field.

Why empty availability does not render as Closed

The first version of this fix dropped the fallback and let an empty array fall
through the normal path, which marked all seven days Closed. Code review
caught that, correctly: it is wrong in the same way the old fallback was
wrong, and worse in effect. The old default at least claimed the photographer
worked weekdays; all-Closed actively tells visitors they are never available.

Empty availability means the hours are unknown, not that the photographer is
closed. Neither state should be invented from an absent field, so the card
says Hours not listed and asserts nothing.

This also keeps the interim state safe. Until the backend change deploys,
availability is absent from every response, so every profile shows
Hours not listed — visibly incomplete, but not misleading.

Deploy order

The backend change must ship first. This PR alone changes what the card
renders when data is absent, but cannot make data appear. Merging it without
the backend replaces one wrong display with an empty one.

Verification

  • ./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit — exit 0.
  • ./node_modules/.bin/eslint src/components/photographer-profile.tsx — exit 0.
    Both run after merging origin/master through #28, so they reflect the
    current flat ESLint config rather than the one this branch forked from.
  • Backend data confirmed against the dedicated availability endpoint, which
    already exposed the same rows the dashboard reads:
    GET /v1/photographers/curtis-lloyd-mgs8/availability returns all seven
    days, lowercase.
  • Not yet verified end to end: the profile page cannot show real days until
    the backend change is deployed. After deploy, load
    /photographer/curtis-lloyd-mgs8 and confirm all seven days render as Open,
    matching the dashboard and the photographer_availabilities rows for that
    photographer.

Description:

Adjust the Next.js dynamic routing pattern for city landing pages to follow the required URL structure (/360-virtual-tour-photographer-[city]) and render the exact H1 format.

Acceptance Criteria:

  1. Support the route pattern /360-virtual-tour-photographer-[city-slug] (e.g., /360-virtual-tour-photographer-toronto).

  3. Fetch and display photographers located in the requested city.
